source.title: What is the functional role of SAE errors?

record.tranche_reason: The post uses causal ablation and restoration experiments to test whether SAE error nodes carry information used in model computation, a different method from the original study's error-predictability and scaling analyses.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own ablation, restoration, faithfulness, and probing outcomes. It also discusses cross-layer superposition and derived features as hypotheses, but does not directly separate linear from nonlinear SAE error or measure error scaling across SAE sizes. Background results and claims attributed to other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The post ablates residual error nodes in a Gemma-2 2B sparse feature circuit (SVA-RC) and measures the loss of circuit faithfulness. That bears directly on V5, whether feature-based circuit analyses lose behaviour without the error term. It does not measure error predictability, scaling, loss versus random errors, or training-objective effects.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors find that ablating residual error nodes destroys circuit performance, yet restoring a narrow group of late-mid SAE features fully mitigates it. They propose cross-layer superposition as one hypothesis, with intermediate or redundant features as alternatives. They judge their results to somewhat lower the probability of a separate 'path through the error nodes'. They identify layers 11-18 as critical and caution about self-repair and feature baselines. Their crosscoder training failed, and the probing results were inconclusive.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses sparse feature circuit attribution, error-node ablation and feature restoration, plus linear probing; it does not apply the original study's measurements of linear error predictability or error scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes depend on layer range, token position, mean versus zero ablation, feature-restoration range and count, and whether the earlier 'that' token is also ablated.

fits_no_version.finding: The effect of ablating error nodes on behaviour can be fully undone by restoring clean values of a small set of late-mid (layers 16-21) SAE features. This suggests the error's function is mediated through downstream SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The functional contribution of SAE error nodes in circuits is largely routed through a few downstream SAE features, consistent with cross-layer superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes trained on the layer-19 SAE error recover basic features and XORs. With logistic regression they do not beat residual-stream probes. Steering with error-trained truth probes works worse than with other probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SAE error term linearly encodes task-relevant (including derived XOR) information, but no more than the residual stream.

record.problems: Preliminary, single-model SVA-RC circuit evidence; results rely heavily on ablation and approximate attribution, and the authors note the Hydra/self-repair effect. Some findings are only described qualitatively from figures. The authors also report noisy ablation effects and say their feature baselines may be flawed. Crosscoder training was unsuccessful, and the post does not directly isolate error components.
record.rows_left_out: Individual cells and additional combinations in the restoration and ablation-threshold plots were not separately recorded where the text gives no distinct readable outcome or value; see Ablation and restoration experiments and Ablation heatmap. Background results attributed to other studies were also omitted.

untested.parts: No measurement of the linearly predictable share of the error. A commenter suggests this split but it was not run.
No comparison of error norms across SAE sizes or contexts.
No comparison of reconstruction error with random errors of the same norm.
Linear and nonlinear error components are not separated. The cross-layer superposition and derived-feature hypotheses are only discussed, and probing was inconclusive.
Only one task (SVA-RC), one model (Gemma-2 2B) and one SAE family (Gemma Scope residual SAEs). Steering analyses were not tested for error dependence.
No comparison of SAE architectures or objectives. The crosscoder attempt failed in training.

missing.what: Expanding window with the left boundary fixed at 0: faithfulness declines gradually, with a sharp drop at layer 18, and reaches zero only in late-layer ranges.
missing.locator: Targeted error ablation; Expanding window ablation; Sliding right boundary

missing.what: The last error node is particularly important: no restored layer range mitigates the effect of ablating it.
missing.locator: Ablation heatmap, discussion of T=24 vs T=23

missing.what: Faithfulness-vs-circuit-size curves on the outlier-filtered dataset, with residual or MLP/Attn error nodes ablated. The 1K-node circuit has F=0.526 after filtering.
missing.locator: Notes on the key metrics; Faithfulness metric

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label is removed. Feature restoration patches clean feature values that already encode the error's upstream contribution, so it does not show that feature-only analyses retain behaviour without the error term. Those rows are reclassified as mechanism evidence (fits_no_version). The evidence is a preliminary single-circuit Alignment Forum post, and many results are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure what share of the error vector is linearly predictable from the input activation.
Does not compare per-token error norms across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same tokens, or whether error persists with scale.
Does not compare model loss from SAE reconstructions with random errors of the same size.
Does not distinguish linearly predictable and nonlinear error components or test their proposed feature content and learnability separately.
Tests error-node contributions in one Gemma-2 2B subject-verb-agreement circuit and related probing tasks; does not evaluate a broad set of circuits, steering analyses, models, or behaviors.
Does not compare SAE training objectives, architectures, or end-to-end training as ways to reduce dark matter.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated residual error nodes at the last token up to the second-to-last layer, without restoring features.
rows.note: The post gives 0.13 as the faithfulness when no features are restored after this ablation.
rows.check: Ablating all last-token residual error nodes up to layer 23 drops faithfulness to 0.13, a near-complete loss. That is V5's effect in full, not partial. The baseline is the unablated circuit, F=1 by construction.

source_check.correct: Mean-ablate last-token residual errors through layer 23; leave layers 24 and 25 unablated; restore no features; faithfulness 0.13.
source_check.problem: The source inconsistently says second-to-last layer, but its explicit specification excludes both layers 24 and 25; use through layer 23.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: After residual error-node ablation, restored the top-1 layer-18 SAE feature, the Plural subject feature.
rows.note: The authors say restoring this single feature does nothing.
rows.check: This is a mechanism probe. It restores clean SAE feature values with error ablated. It does not measure how much behaviour is lost without the error term, so it does not bear on V5.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: After residual error-node ablation, restored layer-18 SAE features ranked by AtP score.
rows.note: The post describes this as a substantial but incomplete recovery.
rows.check: Restoration experiment. It shows where the error's influence is mediated, not whether a feature-only analysis loses behaviour. Patching clean feature values bypasses the error's upstream role.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B

rows.locator: Alternative interpretations; Ablation and restoration experiments
rows.note: The authors report the range for top-25 feature restoration and describe it as short of full restoration.
rows.check: Restoration experiment (0.13 to 0.75-0.85). Same issue as r5: it does not measure V5's quantity.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B

rows.note: The authors describe this as rough evidence that error-node information is more task-specific.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B

rows.locator: Targeted error ablation; Expanding window ablation; Conclusions
rows.note: The authors identify layers 11-18 as the critical region; ablating this range brings faithfulness down to 0.3.
rows.check: Ablating error nodes in layers 11-18 alone drops faithfulness to 0.3, a large loss. 'Observed' fits better than partial. The row's baseline is unablated faithfulness (1).

relationships.condition: Gemma-2 2B SVA-RC circuit, mean-ablating residual error nodes across mid layers
relationships.reason: Residual error ablation destroys faithfulness to 0.13, the 11-18 range alone drops it to 0.3, and the layer-24 error node matters (r1, r3, r11, r13, r17, r18).
relationships.display_finding: Ablating residual errors reduced faithfulness to 0.13, ablating layers 11–18 alone reduced it to 0.3, and the layer-24 error also mattered.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Gemma-2 2B SVA-RC circuit, mean-ablating residual error nodes across mid layers
source_check.reason: Faithfulness falls to 0.13 without restoration and to 0.3 for layers 11–18; layer-24 ablation also reduces faithfulness under specified restoration conditions. These establish meaningful functional dependence, although r13 alone is partial.

relationships.condition: Error nodes in late layers (18-25 windows), short early-mid windows, and MLP/Attention error nodes
relationships.reason: Late-layer error windows have little effect, 4-layer early-mid windows keep faithfulness above 0.7, and MLP/Attention error ablation is much less destructive (r2, r14, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Late-layer error ablations had little effect, four-layer early-middle ablations retained faithfulness above 0.7, and MLP or attention error ablations were much less destructive.

relation.reason: The post reports its own interventions measuring how much subject–verb agreement performance depends on SAE error nodes.

tranche.reason: Circuit faithfulness under error ablation and feature restoration directly tests V5 using a different method from error predictability and scaling measurements.

source_check.notes: Subsequent ablation experiments use samples filtered by full-model logit difference >4, retaining 16,433 of 50,538 samples. Feature restoration can fully mitigate the specified residual-error ablation; self-repair and uncertain feature baselines limit mechanistic conclusions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Residual error-node ablation and the reported critical layer ranges in the SVA-RC circuit
reader_labels.reason: Ablating residual error nodes is more destructive than ablating MLP and Attention error nodes, and ablating error nodes in layers 14-17 or the expanding 11-18 range substantially harms faithfulness (r1, r3, r13, r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Error-node ablation confined to later layers
reader_labels.reason: Ablating later error-node windows has very little effect, so the reported contribution is not uniform across layers (r14).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Restoring SAE features can substantially or completely recover faithfulness while error nodes remain ablated, including recovery to 1 in reported conditions; this qualifies the claim that error must be kept for the behavior to be retained (r7, r9, r12).
